extracted.intended_audience: researchers asked to serve as peer reviewers/referees for Life Science Alliance (life-science/biomedical manuscripts)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for academic referees reviewing life-science and biomedical manuscripts submitted to the journal Life Science Alliance, covering criteria for publication, report writing, confidentiality, conflicts of interest, and procedural steps in the online system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance and importance of the findings to the specific field
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts are critically evaluated for advance and importance of the findings to the specific field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LSA publishes high-quality research across the life sciences; manuscripts are assessed for whether findings represent an advance and are important to the relevant field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong evidence for the conclusions that are drawn
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts are critically evaluated for strong evidence for the conclusions that are drawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees should judge whether the presented data actually support the authors' conclusions; emphasis on rigorous support for claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referee reports should set out clear, substantiated arguments and concrete recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: The most useful referee reports are those that set out clear, substantiated arguments and concrete recommendations for the improvements and experiments necessary to achieve suitability for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial decisions are based on the strengths of the arguments raised by each referee rather than counting votes; provide concrete, actionable advice for authors and editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include all comments pertinent to scientific evaluation in the referee report (no confidential comments to the editor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Life Science Alliance does not ask for 'confidential comments to the editor'; instead, referees are asked to include all comments pertinent to the scientific evaluation of the manuscript in the referee report itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that all scientific criticisms and suggestions are stated within the main report so authors and editors see them; only truly urgent issues that cannot be included (ethics/data integrity/biosecurity/conflicts) should be emailed to the editor separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate urgent ethical/data/biosecurity/conflicts directly to the editor
rubrics_metrics.description: Urgent further issues that cannot be included in the referee report, in particular, concerns about ethical standards, data integrity, biosecurity or conflicts of an academic or commercial nature, can and should be communicated directly to the editor via email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a concern is urgent or cannot be properly conveyed in the public report, contact the editorial office immediately using email rather than hiding it in a confidential field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide cross-comments on other referees' reports promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: Life Science Alliance routinely asks referees to comment on each other's reports. As soon as all reports have been received, all referees have two days to consider the other referees' views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the two-day window to scrutinize extreme opinions, detect mistakes, and help editors reach balanced decisions; cross-commenting improves fairness and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: When relevant, be clear about what revision is required for acceptability and justify arguments thoroughly
rubrics_metrics.description: Care should be taken to avoid factually incorrect statements and to thoroughly justify arguments in favor or disfavour of any given study. We also encourage referees to be as clear as possible about what revision will be required for a manuscript to become acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to make it apparent to the author and the editor how to proceed without need for additional consultation; justify major criticisms with evidence and specify experiments or changes needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referee selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Referee selection is based on many factors, including expertise, reputation, specific recommendations, and previous experience with the referee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors avoid using referees excluded by authors and avoid referees who have repeatedly provided reports of low quality or delayed reports. Editors contact referees about the possibility first and expect confidentiality from invitees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate actions upon receipt of a manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receiving a manuscript for review: check the quality of the PDF/figures; double-check the deadline; skim the manuscript and consider conflicts of interest; read the editor's letter carefully and note any specific points requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the editorial office immediately if there are problems with file quality, deadline misunderstandings, or potential conflicts; early triage avoids unnecessary delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality: do not discuss the manuscript outside the review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees should treat the review process as strictly confidential and should not discuss manuscripts with anyone not directly involved in the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If colleagues are consulted, they should be identified to the editors in the submission system. If outside experts are consulted, check with editors beforehand to avoid involving excluded individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer anonymity and identity disclosure policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees should, as a rule, not disclose their identities to the authors or to other colleagues. Should they feel strongly about making their identities known to the authors, they can sign their report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors strongly disapprove of attempts by authors to determine the identities of referees; referees are encouraged not to confirm or deny such speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on uploading manuscripts to LLMs/generative AI that ingest user input
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are prohibited from uploading a manuscript to large language models (LLMs), or other generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies that ingest user input for model training, noting this excludes most publicly available AI/LLM tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uploading manuscripts to such AI tools represents a breach of confidentiality; do not submit manuscript text, figures, or data to third-party AI systems that may retain or train on input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus of evaluation: significance and conclusiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Referee evaluations should mainly focus on the significance and conclusiveness of the study at hand, i.e. whether the findings and conclusions at the current stage might be considered sufficiently important for the field in principle, and whether the presented data actually support these conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees are prompted to assess these points directly via rating options and to indicate whether they would need to see an eventual revised version before acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a positive, impartial, but critical tone; avoid offensive language
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees are asked to maintain a positive and impartial, but critical, attitude. Criticisms should remain dispassionate; offensive language is not acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negative reports should explain the weaknesses so authors understand the basis for requests for revision or rejection; positive reports should explain why the study is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report: initial summary paragraph with overall impressions and major shortcomings
rubrics_metrics.description: The ideal report should include an initial paragraph that summarises the major findings and the referee's overall impressions, as well as highlighting major shortcomings of the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This high-level summary helps editors and authors quickly understand the main strengths and problems before delving into numbered comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report: use specific numbered comments (major and minor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific numbered comments, which may be broken down into major and minor criticisms if appropriate (numbering facilitates both the editor's evaluation of the manuscript and the authors' rebuttal to the report).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbered, categorized comments make it easier for authors to prepare a point-by-point response and for editors to track issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report should explicitly answer key evaluative questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The report should answer the following questions: What are the major claims and how significant are they? Are the claims convincing? Are the claims appropriately discussed in the context of earlier literature? Is the study of interest? Are there other experiments that would strengthen the paper?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address these questions directly in your report to help editors and authors understand the basis for your judgment and suggested next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide constructive advice for manuscripts meriting further consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: For manuscripts that may merit further consideration, it is helpful if referees provide advice on clarity of writing, shortening the manuscript, avoiding overselling the claims, representing earlier literature fairly, improving methodological detail for reproducibility, and submission of supplementary data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of useful supplementary data include crystallographic information, source code for modeling, microarray data, detailed methods, mathematical derivations, long tables and movies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not include a direct publication recommendation in the author report
rubrics_metrics.description: This author report should not include a direct recommendation regarding publication, as the final decision regarding acceptance, revision or rejection rests with the editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus the report on evaluation and required changes rather than a binary publication recommendation for the authors; editors will use reports and their judgment to decide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing and moderation of referee reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors do not suppress referee reports. On rare occasions, reports may be edited with permission where the referee has made a mistake, or to remove offensive language or comments that reveal confidential information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid making statements that may cause offense or be libelous. Editors may intervene to remove problematic language or confidential disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees should respond promptly or inform the editorial office if they anticipate significant delay, which allows the journal to keep authors informed and, where necessary, find alternative referees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely communication preserves the efficiency of the editorial process and benefits authors and the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest: disclosure and avoidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees should draw attention to anything that might affect their report, including competing work or commercial interests, and decline to referee in cases where they feel unable to be objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors try to avoid referees with recent/ongoing collaborations with the authors, who have commented on drafts, are in direct competition, have a history of dispute, or have a financial interest in the outcome. However, prior review of the paper for another journal is not necessarily an exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alert editors to breaches of publication policy or ethical conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees who are familiar with the field are more likely to recognise breaches such as plagiarism or author conflicts of interest and should alert the editors to any potential problems either by e-mail or using the confidential comments to the editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raise suspected ethical issues quickly and provide evidence or rationale so the editors can investigate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback to referees and handling of re-reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Journal policy is to ask referees for cross-comments on each other's reports and to inform all referees of the editorial decision. When referees are asked to re-review a revised manuscript, they will receive copies of all the original comments of all reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect to see other reviewers' original comments and the decision rationale when participating in re-review; use this context to judge whether authors adequately addressed concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Navigating the online system and procedural instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Manuscript screen has two tabs: (1) Manuscript Files and Details; (2) Link to referee guidelines & Review form including general ratings, co-referee box, review text box. Reviewers may download/print the PDF, draft their review offline, and paste it back into the online text area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If working offline, carefully check after copying/pasting that all text transferred correctly; the system provides help dialogs and the editorial office can be contacted for further assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration checklist for evaluations: originality
rubrics_metrics.description: In your evaluation you may want to consider: Is the paper original?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge novelty relative to existing literature and whether the work provides new insights or methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration checklist for evaluations: writing quality
rubrics_metrics.description: In your evaluation you may want to consider: Is it well written?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess clarity, organization, readability, and whether the narrative appropriately presents the study and conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration checklist for evaluations: references
rubrics_metrics.description: In your evaluation you may want to consider: Are critical references given?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether the manuscript cites and discusses the most relevant prior work and places findings in proper context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration checklist for evaluations: length commensurate with message
rubrics_metrics.description: In your evaluation you may want to consider: Is the length of the paper commensurate with the message?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the manuscript is concise and contains the appropriate level of detail for its claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration checklist for evaluations: necessity of tables/figures/graphs/photos
rubrics_metrics.description: In your evaluation you may want to consider: Are all tables, figures, graphs, and photographs necessary?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether each visual element contributes materially to the arguments and could be combined, simplified, or moved to supplementary material if redundant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration checklist for evaluations: Materials and Methods adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: In your evaluation you may want to consider: If applicable, is 'Material and Methods' section adequately written and referenced?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether methodological descriptions are sufficient for reproducibility and whether references or additional methodological detail are needed; suggest specific additions if required.
